utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody around the court. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Aditya Menon and Daryl Mundis for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends from the OTP. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic, with legal assistant Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yesterday, before you started testifying, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ribo. I hope you have had a good rest and that we will bring this to a close today. I have still a number of questions to ask of you, and I kindly ask you to answer my questions as directly as possible and as concisely as possible. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's start from Exhibit D1033.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I meant Exhibit 104, 104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... because I thought we saw D1033 yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, please direct your attention to this page. Are you able to read the names there?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, therefore, you see the names on the list?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first name is Ahmed Ibn Bekir Adilovic. What would your comment be, seeing the names?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names here are not typical of the names normally the Muslims in Bosnia have. Ibn is an Arabic word, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for the first name, Adilovic, is it a Bosnian name which has, in fact, been added the Arabic word, or is it a Bosnian name?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's in fact a Bosnian name to which an Arabic word, in this case "Ibn," has been added.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move to page 20, both in the English and Bosnian versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the page to appear, Mr. Ribo, have you ever seen this document -- or, rather, did you see it when you were at the head of the Travnik TO Staff?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a list of members of the Territorial Defence of the Travnik Sector Staff, so it would appear. Can you tell me, who had the competence of issuing certificates attesting membership of the TO?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the Travnik TO Staff, that's to say my command; in other words, I personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: One could conclude from the title that the Travnik TO Sector Staff was issuing certificates attesting membership of the TO Travnik. Did that body in fact have the competence to issue such certificates?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not, because they did not have a stamp. Everything of the sort should have reached me first. First, I should have received a letter signed by the TO Sector Staff, and then I would place on that document my signature and the stamp that we had had at the TO Staff in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Sector Staff ever -- or Sector Staffs ever issued such certificates?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I saw. I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move to page 30 in both the Bosnian and English versions. There's a list here of several columns. The first contains the ordinal number, the second one the reference number, the third one name and father's name, then the unit of the TO, and then below that it says "Divmusl Snage." What would that mean?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my understanding as a soldier, that would mean sabotage Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did something of the sort exist in the course of 1992 and 1993 within the units of the TO?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing of the sort existed, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Bosnian version be scrolled down a bit to see the name under number 326.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I direct your attention to the name next to the number 326, Camdzic, son of Vahid, Fahir. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. He was the commander of the Mehurici Sector Staff and later on he was the member of the Mehurici Detachment. He was, therefore, one of my commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this person ever a member of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please scroll up now so that we can see the person next to number 300. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 300, you have "Puric, son of Zaim, Midhat." Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was that person ever a member of the Muslim forces or Muslim sabotage forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, a series of leading questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't see that that's a leading question if I am asking the witness whether he knows a given individual or not, but let me take it differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, you said you know Midhat Puric, son of Zaim. To your knowledge, he was a member of which unit?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Midhat Puric was never a member of the Muslim forces. He was a commander of the smaller units of the Patriotic League in Gluha Bukovica in the right flank -- the further-most right flank of the units within my AOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can put the document away, unless the Judges have any questions in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do have a question, ma'am. Looking at the heading of this document, it's titled that it's membership certificates of some TO people of Travnik, if I remember the title well. I haven't seen any certificate. I've been seeing -- I'm just seeing a list, and I would like to -- and I did hear you, Madam Vidovic, asking the witness, at the beginning of -- at the introduction of this document, asking whether anybody had the competence to issue certificates, and the witness said only he could. Where are these certificates that you are talking about, Mr. Ribo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The very title states that it's a list of members of the Sector Staff of Travnik for whom certificates of their TO membership were issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go back to --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- Page 1. Now I want page 1, where the heading is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, that's at page 20 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's go to that page, then. Right. Now, the English says: "List of Territorial Defence Regional Staff members, Municipal Territorial Defence Staff, Travnik, issued with the Territorial Defence Travnik Municipality membership certificates." Now, I'm not quite sure whether, from this list, this Court can conclude that these people were issued with certificates, unless we see examples of those certificates. This is just a list, and I think that's the point I'm making.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my answer: Certificates are issued directly to the requesting individual. They are not kept within the Staff. Normally, individuals asked for such certificates when they have to go out into the field, and for that purpose they are issued directly to the requesting individual. That's my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would imagine that the office would retain some copy of sorts of the certificate. It doesn't?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't keep copies of these certificates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us clarify this further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that had you issued such certificates, you would have kept a list of individuals who had been given the certificates in the TO Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond, I said "would that have been the case, would you or would you have not," and that's the same formula of questioning that the Prosecutor had been using throughout his case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, when the Prosecutor asked questions like that, you should have objected. The question should be -- now, let me see -- the question you should have asked was: "If you had issued the certificates, what would you have done?" That's the question you should have asked. Now, to say that, "Because you did it, therefore I'm entitled to do it" is not Defence," Madam Vidovic, so I rule that question out of order, that it is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I will rephrase. But I believe that it was misinterpreted, my question, there was a mistranslation. I will put my next question now. Allow me to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you or did you not keep the lists of individuals to whom certificates were issued, if they were in fact issued?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't keep them in the Staff, for the simple reason that there was a lot of paperwork around and it would have been far too much work and filing and so on and so forth. Had the -- if the Travnik Sector Staff commander sent us lists, we would not have kept them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the commander of the Sector Staff of Travnik ever send to you the list that you can see before you now?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, obviously when the counsel and the witness speak the same language, it's extremely difficult to place any objections on the record, because, quite frankly, by the time the interpretation comes, the question has been answered. I would ask if the witness could be instructed to pause between question and answer and perhaps to watch the screen so that we can timely put objections on the record. I will reiterate that we will argue, at the conclusion of all of the evidence, that little, if any, weight should be given to answers that stem from leading questions on direct examination, as I'm sure my learned colleagues will be doing the same thing with respect to the Prosecution case. I want to make it very clear that it's not always possible to make a timely objection because the witness and counsel speak the same language, so I want to make it absolutely clear what our position will be at the completion of this case with respect to leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, may I just request you to pause after counsel has asked you a question before you answer. You see, both of you speak the same language. We don't hear -- we don't understand what you're saying to each other. We wait for the interpretation. And therefore you're always ahead of us. We would like you to wait for us so that if there is any intervention we would like to make, we are able to make that intervention. Okay? Thank you very much. I'll ask of you the same, Madam Vidovic; after the witness has answered, to pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I will ask you a different question now. We can put this document away. Did you know an individual by the name of Mehmed Alagic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when was it that you first came in touch with him, if you ever came in touch with him?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in the month of November, toward the end of my term of service as the commander of the Travnik TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to him at the time, and if so, did he tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: November which year, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I asked you if you talked with him then when you met him for the first time, and if you did, did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke with him very briefly, because he arrived in the convoy with refugees. And he happened to be at my command post, and he asked about the 17th Krajiska Brigade in order to join it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what happened after that with General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, after that he was placed in the Travnik barracks and he was training or preparing the sniper unit. After that, after a certain amount of time, because he was a former JNA lieutenant colonel, he became the commander of the Bosanska Krajina Operations Group, and after that he became the commander of the 3rd Corps and then the commander of the 7th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you know when the operations groups were formed?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe this was in October.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. It's very hard for me to remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ribo, do you remember when Jajce fell into Serb hands?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was in September or October.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, did Mehmed Alagic have or not have any kind of role in the events relating to Jajce?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he didn't have any role, because he simply wasn't in the territory of the Travnik Municipality at the time, where I was the commander, so I'm not aware of him having any role in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move to a different topic. I would like to ask you something -- I would like to see what you know about Afro-Asian armed people, if you have any knowledge about that, and I would like to ask you this: Did you know that in the Travnik region, there were such armed people of Afro-Asia origin at the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "1993," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were performing your duties as the TO Staff commander, did you meet any of these people?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not meet any of these people as TO Staff commander, and no Afro-Asian person with weapons or uniform entered my Staff or headquarters in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this first: Did you have any knowledge that they were there in that area?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard from people, from fighters, that there was some foreigners, but I think that even at that time, I didn't know that they had weapons, that they were kind of half soldiers, wearing soldiers' jackets at the top and traditional Arab wear at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And among those people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I apologise for interjecting. It seems to be a bit unclear, from the question as reflected on lines 11 through 15 and the interpreter's correction on line 16, whether we're talking about the period of 1992 or 1993, and I would ask if that could be clarified, perhaps, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you'll remember, Mr. Ribo, I asked you if, in the Travnik area in the period of 1992 and 1993, according to what you know, if there were any Afro-Asians in that area at that time. Do you recall me asking you that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my work as the TO Travnik Staff commander, no Afro-Asian person in uniform and weapons entered my headquarters or any of my commands in the Travnik area. I did hear from the local population and fighters that there were such soldiers who were half soldiers, let's say. They were wearing a soldier's camouflage jacket at the top, and the bottom was traditional Arab wear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. What I want to ask you is this: The TO Travnik Staff in the village of Mehurici, did it have a unit there or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The TO Staff did have a regional -- a sector staff in the village of Mehurici, and it was headed by Candzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And where was this staff located?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from the overview of my unit that I provided to the Defence Ministry in 1995 that it was located in the elementary school of Mehurici. It was a small command. It had seven or eight people. So it was at the lower part of the Mehurici School, and it had only three rooms for its use, one commander's office, one meeting hall, and a small kitchenette.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us, if you know, how that Mehurici Detachment got the use of those rooms in the Mehurici School? Who granted them that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sector Staff of Mehurici were allowed to use those premises by the National Defence Secretariat of the Municipality of Travnik, because we asked to have that area allocated for the use of our Sector Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, once again, this National Defence Secretariat, is this a civilian or a military body?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a civilian organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Please, during your duties as Staff commander, did you ever visit that Mehurici Staff or headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity -- did you or did you not have the opportunity to see these foreigners in that area?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see those foreigners, but I did have the remark by my Sector Staff in Mehurici commander that in that area, in the Mehurici settlement, there were some Afro-Asians milling around in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information from anyone that they were located at the school?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assistant training chief, an operations chief, said that there was information, I think this was in late July, that during the night, around 2200 hours, the rooms in the Mehurici area were toured by Adil Lozo and Aganovic, Zihnija, and when they met with the school director they were asked, "What are you doing," they said they were just simply looking at the school in order to billet a unit there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Can you please just tell us, at that time, what were Adil Lozo and Zihnija Aganovic doing, if they were doing anything and if you know? I'm thinking of what their profession was, what their job was at the time.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zihnija Aganovic was the commander of the Regional Staff of the Patriotic League, and in a way he was a member of the government, of the District Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Adil Lozo?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adil Lozo was a lawyer, and he was his associate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "associate," can you please tell us where he worked?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now I really don't know where Adil Lozo was working.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, very well. Now, you said, from what I understood, that these people were looking to accommodate the Mujahedin somewhere, and do you know, were these Mujahedin billeted at that school or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were billeted at that school, but only the Command. I think that they were their officers. I don't know exactly what duties they had, so a small number of them were billeted at the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now let me ask you this: At the time you were the TO commander, could you in any way have had any influence or not on the fact whether those people would be billeted at the school or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I could not have any influence on that, just like the Muslim forces, I couldn't have any influence on the Patriotic League either. Anyone could form whatever they wanted and could do whatever they wanted. It was the most difficult situation for me. I had to hold the lines of defence. I didn't have time to be dealing with these people who were lazing around, lying around, resting, provoking, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of 1992, did you hear of a person called "Abu Abdel Aziz" or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear the name, but I never saw that man, not in 1992 or never in the course of the war did I see that man.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like to move to another group of questions. I would like to ask you about the El Mudjahedin Detachment. But before that: Did you ever meet or encounter British journalist Andrew Hogg?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't meet him, and I didn't talk to him either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I am going to ask you some questions about the El Mudjahedin Detachment. When you were giving us your particulars, you said that you were the commander of the 301st Brigade in the period from November 1992 until the 30th of November, 1993, and that in that capacity, you occasionally attended meetings at the 3rd Corps Command. Do you recall that? So let me ask you this: Did you, in that period, attend meetings at the Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was the commander of the 301st Mechanised Brigade at that time, and I did attend meetings for various reasons, in order to report back, issue assignments, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in that period of a year from late 1992 to late 1993, did anyone from the El Mudjahedin Detachment attend any of those meetings in that period?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really recall that never -- no foreigner attended these briefings or meetings, including any of the people from the El Mujahid or El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the witness now please look at D968.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, first of all, I would like to say for the transcript that this is an order of the 3rd Corps Command of the 28th of August, 1994, and that the document is headed: "Field inspection of the 3-Sjever/North," or G Group? Can you see and read this document, Mr. Ribo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask something, is this document of the 28th or 29th of August? The interpretation says 28th, the document says the 29th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 29th, Your Honour. It's possible that I made a slip, and if I did, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can you look at paragraph two. It talks about the field inspection of the units, and your name is mentioned, the name "Ribo, Haso" is mentioned. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the document, this team was supposed to tour the units of the 7th Muslim and the El Mudjahedin Detachment. First of all, do you remember this situation?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your assignment, specifically, then?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assignment was to tour the units, according to the order, to gauge the situation on the lines attained, and to observe the weaknesses and the linkage of the units on the line. And if there were any problems and weaknesses, we were supposed to eliminate the weaknesses, and of course our objective was, since combat was forthcoming, to establish whether combat documents were being drafted in those units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you manage to carry out your assignment or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I partially carried out the assignment. I toured the 7th Muslim -- Glorious Muslim Brigade, but I did not tour the Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you could not really go and visit anything that had to do with them. You couldn't establish anything, make any counts or anything like that. They didn't allow that. So when I returned to the OG North command post, I informed the commander of that operations group, and of course the chief of staff, when I returned to the corps, that I was not able to completely execute my assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit 1185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This, of course, is essential to the case, so I think we should ask the witness if he could dwell a little more on the evidence he gave about the access to the Mujahedin in Mehurici, I understand. He said, and I quote: "They didn't allow that." What does that mean? Who did not allow it, and did he try, and what happened? Can you explain a little more about the meetings that you had with the Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have any meetings with the El Mujahid Detachment. If you look at the list, I can tell you that the four persons who were there, all of them were ex-JNA officers. In the El Mujahid Detachment, there were those members who were extremists and who were local people, Bosniaks, and they knew who we were and what we were, and we were simply not allowed access to their command or the area where they were. The four individuals who toured and inspected the 7th Muslim Unit and who were tasked with touring the El Mujahid were professional soldiers of the former JNA, and it was on that basis that we were not allowed access, because they fully distrusted the former JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. But do you remember actually how this happened, what happened? Were you there? Did you come to the gate, front gate, of the Mujahid camp and ask to get in and were told, "No," or can you be more specific? Just what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. This was out in the field. It was their camp, and of course they had their guards, as is the case with any military encampment, they have their guards around. When we announced our visit and when we approached the guards, this camp was above the Serici village in the Teslic theatre of war, in the direction of Teslic, because the OG North units were deployed and engaged in that -- along that axis. When we approached the guard and explained who we were, he fetched one of the men from the camp. He was an Arab. And after they had a conversation in Arabic, which we didn't understand, they told us that we should turn around and leave, that we were not allowed access into the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And was this the El Mujahid Detachment camp you visited or was it, if you know, another El Mujahid group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that part, this was the El Mujahid unit that was engaged in combat, and it was the right neighbour of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Our assignment was to inspect the units and see what their linkage was in the defence line, how the 7th Muslim was linked up with the El Mujahid Detachment. Of course, they were out on the ground. They had to have tents. And so this unit, although not the entire unit, it was just elements of the unit that was there under tents and so on, it wasn't their place where they were billeted, it was their defence line. It was behind that area where they had a location where men would rest and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. The reason why I'm asking this is we have heard of the presence of other groups of foreign fighters, so I just wanted to make sure that this group that you actually visited was the group that was known as the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was solely the El Mujahid Detachment. There were no other groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you visit the camp where they were billeted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're referring to that part that was at the battlefield, at the battlefield, I came as far as the guards' post at the perimeter of their camp. If you're referring to the place where they were billeted initially, I never visited that camp ever; not even to this day have I ever been at that location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask one question. Mr. Ribo, this had been an order to you from the 3rd Corps Command. Did you give a written response or a written report of what you did after you visited the Muslim Mountain Brigade and the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't send a written report, because the chief of staff of the corps had given to me this assignment and I orally reported back to him on what I had seen up there. There was no time to write down everything I saw. I was frequently engaged away or out in the field with combat activities, and I didn't have time to write -- to send anything in writing. So what I did was I reported to the corps commander in writing of what I had seen, and I also, on this occasion, reported to the OG commander of the OG North.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. You are interpreted as saying: "So what I did was I reported to the corps commander in writing of what I had seen." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. If you look at item 5 of the order, you will see that members of the team --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you turn to the following page in the English version for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, item 5 clearly states that: Members of the team shall report to the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps, report -- that they will report to him on the situation perceived at the post of the OG North, Sjever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My worry is: You're getting a written instruction, a written order, and you don't respond to it in writing, and on the records of the army, it looks -- it would seem as if this order was either never carried out or never responded to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm invoking item 5 again. After having toured the area, we were duty-bound to report to determine the B/C/S is the "ferisanija" [phoen], which means to normally orally report to your superiors, to the chief of staff of the corps at his command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be helpful, it seems that it's a matter of translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was listening to the interpretation, and I didn't hear a word of what you said, Madam Vidovic. I can only read the English. It says "report," and I see this order is in writing, it's not an oral order. So if it calls for a report, I expect the report must be in writing too. I don't see anything that says "oral" in the English, and I want to believe that this translation here was done by a professional person and therefore it translates correctly what is said in the B/C/S. Otherwise, it shouldn't have been put up here. It should have been corrected -- if the translation is incorrect, it shouldn't have been put up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it would be helpful for the witness to read this out in the Bosnian. This is an official translation, but in the Bosnian original you have the term "referisati." If you look at the Bosnian version, item five, line one, we have the term "referisati," and if the interpreters could interpret that, and we will have the translation corrected. This is the Prosecution Exhibit PT and was officially translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, read out item 5 slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before the witness reads, Madam Vidovic, I've made a statement,. I am saying we have been given documents here and we've been given official translations, and anybody who did the translation should have seen that if this translation is not correct, that it is not correct, and given us a correct translation. We cannot all the time, when we have documents here which are supposed to have been approved by professional translators, then have to rely to people in the court here, who are not professional translators, to tell us how to translate the document. We rely on the English that is being given to us here, and if it is not correct, then we must throw this document out of court until it is properly translated. We have been having this problem right through the trial. Now, I can understand if a document is put up here, it has not been translated, and we ask somebody to translate it. But if we are given a document and we are given its translation, we are bound to rely on the translation, and we cannot accept any corrections that come out in court here by people who are not qualified professional translators.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence should be the last party to be blamed for this, because we, the Defence, have had most of the problems with the translations. These were mostly documents of the Prosecution, the PTs, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am not blaming the Defence. I'm not blaming the Defence. I'm blaming the documents. I'm saying you cannot, at this stage, when we have got an official translation of a document, then want to give us a different meaning out of that document from the meaning that we have been given on the official translation. Otherwise, this document should have been -- before you put it up here, you should have said, "Look, this translation is incorrect. I can't use this thing in its form. I want it properly corrected, properly translated, before I use it."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understand that full well. What I do not understand is how I am expected to do all that with the few people that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you are asking me something that I cannot answer to. Do you realise that? You have employed the people you have to do the job you're supposed to do. If you don't have, you motivate for more people. I don't control your staff, but you have staff that's told you that this B/C/S document is translated into English. Here is the translation. You can see it, yourself, and you can see whether it's correctly translated or not. Now in court you tell us, "No, it is not correctly translated, let's look at the B/C/S." You should have seen that before you put it up, Madam Vidovic, that's what I'm saying, and don't ask me to tell you how you are supposed to do your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question for the witness concerning what happened when you reached this location where the El Mudjahedin Detachment was. I would like to know, did you ask why you were not allowed to enter the camp? Was any justification given to you about this behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no justification was given to me. The guard merely told me to leave the premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you say that you were entitled to enter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I showed the order of the corps chief of staff, but they didn't take any notice of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can I just follow up on the discussion we had just a while ago. On your report please forgive me if I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're not getting the English translation, we're getting something else. It sounded like French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: I got the English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The French interpreter was on the wrong channel. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I apologise. Let me put my question to you again, Mr. Ribo, to return to the issue of the report you gave after having visited the El Mujahid Detachment. You reported to the commander of the 3rd Corps; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I reported to the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. And was it in writing, your report, or was it just oral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an oral report. That's what the order stated. Had they required a written report, they would have stated so in the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, the important thing is not whether your report was written or oral. The important thing is: Do you know what happened to your report? You gave it to the chief of staff, and do you have any idea of what he then did with the information that he received from you about not having been given access to the Mujahid camp? Because, you see, the point we're discussing here is whether information of events that happened on the ground were communicated up towards the top of the system, so that's why I'm asking if you know how the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps handled your information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I know is that I orally reported both to the corps chief of staff and the commander of the OG-3 Sjever or North, and from there it was within the competence of the chief of staff. I don't know what he did as a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I would just like to put one question to you about this, please, the report, "isvesti" [phoen]. You are a professional military man. Can you please tell us whether a report can be written or oral?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, a report can be oral and written. If it's a written report, then it is stressed that a written report should be submitted by such-and-such a time and to whom it should be submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to move to a different topic. I would like to ask you about some events from 1995. Can the witness please look at document D993. For the transcript, it's an order of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina about the appointment to units as of the 31st of March. I would like to ask you to pay attention to the text on page 1 of the Bosnian version. This is page 2 in the English. Under: "3rd Corps," under number 1, there is a name that is stated. Sir, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us to which duties you were appointed pursuant to this order of the 31st of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order appoints me to the Command of the 3rd Corps, to duties of the chief of the organ for operations and training, and I'm also appointed as the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please briefly describe to us what was all part of your duties?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duties were planning, monthly planning, analysis, reporting, then drafting combat documentation, planning combat actions, monitoring combat actions, analysis of combat actions, and then combat training and education, maintaining operations, records. These were mostly my duties in this department.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the drafting of documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that period while you were at this post, were you working on any documents that, among other things, had to do with the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did, but I cannot remember just off the top of my head. I cannot remember all the documents like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become the Exhibit number 1186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown D985, please. D985. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, this is a very brief order. Can you please read it for the transcript? It's an order of the Command of the 3rd Corps of the 9th of January, 1995.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can: "Based on the operations records being messy, resulting in the lack of information on the situation in subordinated units, and for the purpose of obtaining accurate data on the quantities of ammunition and numerical strength of units, I order: "1. You are to submit a complete and accurate overall report on ammunition quantity per unit, broken down by types and unit levels, from battalion to operations groups."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can you please stop here, and can you now look at the end of the document, where you can see that this was delivered to the El Mudjahedin Detachment, among others. Can we please look at page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who is the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, who is the author of this document? His Honour asked.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was drafted in my section, and it was signed by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us who drafted it in your section, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His name is Elvedin Kulelija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this document, I would like to ask you this: Command of the 3rd Corps, did they find it necessary to know, or not, the quantities of ammunition and the exact numerical strength of the units, including the El Mujahid?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was necessary, because the analysis and the operational records containing the number of ammunition, weapons and manpower, was something that was used to gauge the combat readiness of a unit. You have to have records of the exact number of rifles and ammunition and manpower all together, based on which the combat readiness of a unit was gauged and the options in which it can be used in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. You said the document was drafted in your department. I would like to ask you the following: Did you ever receive a report like this, complete and accurate report from the El Mujahedin unit, about the number and quantity of ammunition and the exact number of men in the unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. It's a leading question and it's a compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am going to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, did you ever receive a report as a response to this document of the 9th of January, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received this report. This report never came from the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were at the head of the Department for Operational Planning, did you ever receive a status -- ammunition and weapons status report from the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask you a question. Were you the one who's supposed to receive a report or was it Mahmuljin, the one who should have received this report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the reports are sent to the corps commander or his deputy, the person who also goes through the mail, indicates to whom the document should be given. And in view of the fact that I was at the head of the department maintaining the operations records, this was something that was a part of my department's duties, then a document like this would be addressed to me or sent to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question to ask you, sir. A little earlier, you said that you cannot remember drafting documents in relation to the El Mudjahedin Detachment. Is it not so that perhaps you also don't remember whether you did receive any documents from the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, permit me just something. Your Honours, the witness did not say what you just said. The witness said that he did work, probably, on those documents, but he does not recall any of them unless he sees them. This is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... mean the same thing, and let's go to the sentence that was put to him, his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's page 28, line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. At line 21, page 27, it said: "You mentioned the drafting of documents; is that correct?" "Yes." "Now, in that period, while you were at this post, were you working on any documents that, among other things, had to do with the El Mudjahedin Detachment?" "I probably did, but I cannot remember just off the top of my head." Now, how different is that from what I said to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, from what I understood, and at least that is the translation that I received, you told the witness if he could not -- that he could not recall working on the documents, but he actually said something else. He said, "I probably did, but I just cannot recall off the top of my head." So I understood it differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough. Yes, I didn't say he probably did, I just said he didn't remember, which is the gravamen of his answer to your question, he doesn't remember. And I'm just asking him how he remembers receiving any or not receiving any reports from the El Mudjahedin Detachment, if he doesn't remember, from the top of his head, that he ever drafted documents. That's all I'm asking. The one situation, he doesn't remember. The other situation, he seems to be very clear that he remembers not receiving anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you explain this now? Can you give an answer to His Honour on this question?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether I did or did not work on a document if I don't see it. Thus, I did not work on this document. It was done by an officer in my department. But all the post, in its circulation, first goes to the head of the department, it doesn't go to the person drafting the documents, it goes to the chief. And then in my section, I would indicate precisely to whom the post should go, and that means the person that drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, please, can you answer the question put by His Honour? You recall in one situation, and in another situation, you don't. So when we're talking about reports from the El Mudjahedin Detachment, why, if you remember, why do you remember not receiving this?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I never received a written report from the El Mujahid Detachment. You can check this anywhere. I never received a single written report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you receive oral reports from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never did meet with them at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break at this stage and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we proceed, just one little point that I notice. If anyone -- all of us can look at the left bottom corner of our screen, we'll see that the name of the witness is spelled as "Rabo," not "Ribo." Can that be corrected? Is there a way of correcting it, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This document, D985, can it please be given an exhibit number, from what I remember?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document D985 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit number 1187.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we leave this document, Madam Vidovic, I would just like to ask the witness if you know who provided the ammunition and the weaponry to the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not aware of that, really. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So I suppose you or the 3rd Corps provided weapons and ammunition to all the other units falling under the 3rd Corps. Did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When I was the staff of the TO Travnik commander, I was not given by the -- a single rifle by the Command or by the Zenica District Staff. In the beginning, we managed however we could. We were buying rifles. Men were buying rifles and the bullets. And then the army grew out from the TO units. If the corps gave anything, I don't know, because I was not dealing with the logistics matters. I was dealing with the operational records and record-keeping, not with the issues pertaining to logistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking my question, and I'm putting my reasons to you, so as to enable you to give me a more precise answer, is that if ammunition was provided to the units by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina's system, then of course the 3rd Corps would be entitled also to request from each of these units that they report back to the system of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina just how much ammunition they used. In contrast, if the El Mujahid Detachment got their weapons and their ammunition from somewhere else, that is to say, from outside the ABiH system, then they might have a point in saying that, "We --" or they were not required to report back to the ABiH about the use of their -- and the consumption of their ammunition. Do you see my point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were trying to place the El Mujahid Detachment under the command of the 3rd Corps for all matters. However, this process proceeded with difficulty, and all the information that was requested, it's something that is given in person, information about weapons, ammunition, men. It's not something that is sent by post. There is a book of operational records in all subordinate units, and pursuant to this order representatives of commands were supposed to bring this information or representatives of units were supposed to give that to me at the Staff so that I could copy it into my book from their books. But as I said, the El Mujahid Detachment never appeared with these records or with any other records, so we could never establish how many of them there were, where they were getting their weapons from, where they were getting ammunition from, even where the food they had was coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. And just to conclude, we are sure, are we not, that the orders were, in fact, sent to and received by the El Mujahid Detachment, the orders to report back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Orders were sent to them, but I never received any written or oral reports from that unit, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness now please look at D1014. For the transcript, it's a document of the 3rd Corps Command, conclusions and tasks from the consultative meeting of the senior officers of the armoured mechanised units, achievements analysis, dated the 9th of August, 1995. Can we now look at page 2 of this document, please, where we can see the signature. This is page 4 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you know who signed this document? Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was signed by the 3rd Corps chief of staff, Colonel Kedir Jusic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this document before? Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see this document earlier, but this is because it was drafted by my colleague, who took over the duties from me, and he consulted me about the drafting of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go back to the first page, please, both in the Bosnian and the English versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I'm going to ask you to look at paragraph marked 1, and can we look at this paragraph both in the English and Bosnian versions. I'm going to quote just a short part of this paragraph. I think it's the second sentence of this paragraph 1. It says: "In the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps, in the most recent combat operations at the Vozuca front, a T-55 was captured, and for the time being it is given to the 3rd Tank Company, although its status has not been finally resolved, considering that it is war booty of the El Mudjahedin Detachment." Please, can you comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you ask the question, Madam Vidovic, you referred the witness to paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I hear being translated is not what I read on paragraph 1 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was paragraph marked "1", so with the number 1, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that that should be the sentence beginning: "In the most recent combat operations ..." Item 1, the sentence starting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's the sentence in the middle of the paragraph. I'm looking at the beginning of the paragraph. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can you please comment on this passage of the document? You said that you were consulted in the drafting of the document.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can comment on it. What it has to do with is T-55 that was captured by El Mujahid. It was war booty that was captured on that front, and its status was never resolved, because we had armoured mechanised units in the corps, we had the 3rd Tank Company and the 37th Tank Company that were part of the 37th Division, and the 3rd Tank Company was within -- was attached to the Corps Command. The status of the tank was not resolved, because the El Mujahid never allowed the tank to be handed over to the 3rd Tank Company in order for it to become property of the 3rd Tank Company rather than their property.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Corps Command ask for the tank to be handed over?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we did. We could not even begin to understand that they would have a tank without being able to use it. However, we intervened several times. The chief of armoured units and I, we intervened, asking that the tank be handed over to the 3rd Tank Company, but this matter was never resolved because they refused to hand the tank over.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, just that last statement by the witness confuses me. He says: "But this matter was never resolved because they refused to hand the tank over." But this document says it was, for the time being, given to the 3rd Tank Company, so it must have been handed over to be given over to the 3rd Tank Company. Are you able to explain that, Mr. Ribo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't handed over to the 3rd Tank Company. Rather, the men from the 3rd Tank Company --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat that part of his answer, because the interpreter didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... But all the way through to the end of the war, they never handed the tank over. It was never listed in the records of the 3rd Tank Company as their asset, as their property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That may be so, but the tank, physically, according to this document, was, if I may use the words used there, given to the 3rd Tank Company for the time being. I don't know how long the "time being" lasted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't given to the 3rd Tank Company; rather, the men, the crew from the 3rd Tank Company manned the tank. But the tank itself was still part of the El Mujahid Detachment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So what you are saying --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- by location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What you're saying is that this document is incorrect, because it clearly says, and I'm reading the English here, it clearly says: " ... And for the time being it is given to the 3rd Tank Company." That's what is written there, and I'm saying: Are you saying it is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tank was physically not part of the 3rd Tank Company. It was at the Vozuca front, in the area where it was used by the El Mujahid Detachment. So it was not physically part of the 3rd Tank Company. The tank was not in the same area where the majority of the tanks used by that company were to be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please listen carefully to my question and answer my question. Is this document incorrect where it states that the tank was given to the 3rd Tank Company? Your answer should either be "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1188.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness now look at Exhibit 1029, 1029. For the record, this is a preparatory order of the 3rd Corps Command, dated the 24th March, 1995. Can the witness have a quick look at the second page of the document to look at the signature. That's page 3 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature, perhaps, Mr. Ribo? You're nodding, but you have to state something for the record.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise the signature. It's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Therefore, you signed this document for General Mahmuljin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, please look at item 2.1 of the document, which is page 2 of the English version, page 2 of the English version, item 2.1. Mr. Ribo, I will quote a section of the item: "As part of preparations to be put into combat action, the El Mudjahedin Detachment a task to prepare to be put into action as part of the 3rd or 7th Corps at Vlasic Plateau and go on a march on the following axes: Nemila-Zenica-Ovnak-Vlasic Plateau or Nemila-Zenica-Vitez- Travnik-Galica axis." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall signing the document, and do you recall what item 2.1 referred to?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. At that point in time, Operation Vlasic was in course, and the corps commander and the 3rd Corps chief of staff met with 3rd Corps units at Vlasic Plateau. I was at the command post of the 3rd Corps in Zenica at the time. I received an oral order from the commander of the 3rd Corps to draft an order such as this one for the El Mujahid Detachment to be ready to be deployed within the AOR of the 7th Corps in order to take advantage from successes in combat. I drafted this preparatory order that the unit should be at the ready to be engaged either in the 7th or in the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the El Mudjahedin Detachment follow this order or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mujahid Detachment did not follow the order. It was not engaged in the 7th Corps, because the detachment was always calculating, asking for additional preparation, and in short did not carry out this assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I ask you to keep in mind the date of the document, the 24th of March, 1995. And in the meantime, Your Honours, can this document be assigned -- no, this is already an exhibit. I apologise. Very well. Can we put the document away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm a bit interested in -- sorry, in the reasons why the El Mujahid Detachment did not carry out the orders included here, because they did take part in the overall operation, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recall the El Mujahid Detachment taking part in Operation Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And why not? Not why you don't recall, but did they give any reasons for not wanting to take part in that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They put forward as a reason the fact that they were not ready enough to take part in the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Forgive me for not perhaps understanding this correctly, but there was, as I recall, and I look to the parties to help me out if I have misunderstood, there was a major operation going on in the spring of 1995, and my recollection is that the El Mujahid Detachment did take part in some of it. And here, apparently, is a document that shows that they did not take part in all of it, in this single operation they refused to take part, but please help me out, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have not been discussing Operation Vlasic for a single moment until now. We were dealing with operations at Podsjelovo and the Vozuca area. Vlasic is an area of Travnik, and we have not been dealing with that area so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right, and I apologise for having misunderstood this. So the El Mujahid Detachment was invited to take part, but they refused; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wrote an order to them to be prepared for engagement, but in the later developments they did not take any part in them because they were not prepared to take part in Operation Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And they did not subsequently, at any later point, take part in that operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: How long did the operation last; do you recall? How long did it last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The operation might have lasted one month. I can't be precise. A month, a month and a half. I can't state that with precision, since this was in the AOR of the 7th Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. You told us that they did not take part because they were not sufficiently ready, they were not prepared. They said they were not ready or prepared, so it is themselves who have their reasons for their behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question. I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I shall repeat. They said, themselves, they said to the 3rd Corps that they were not prepared or ready? Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely. They were not prepared or ready to take part in that activity, and they asked for additional time to get prepared, whereas if you want to fit on the successes achieved, you have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. That sentence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I interrupted him, because I was saying that I couldn't hear the interpretation, so I would like the witness to answer from the beginning again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to the El Mujahid Detachment, they refused to carry out the assignment at the Vlasic Plateau because they were not sufficiently ready to take part in the operation, and they sought additional time to get prepared for a offensive activities, whereas the offensive activities at Vlasic required that the unit be immediately engaged in the combat in order to exploit the successes achieved by the units of the 7th Corps. They were simply not prepared to engage in that sort of combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Therefore, I am asking you once again: They gave -- the El Mudjahedin Detachment gave some reasons to justify their behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not simply flatly refuse, without giving reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a moment ago that the reason was that they informed the duty officer in Zenica, at the Zenica command post, that they were not sufficiently ready to be engaged in combat and asked for some additional time to get prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just need to be clarified on one little point, Madam Vidovic, and I did note what you said, that we have not been talking about the Vlasic operation here. But, Witness, Mr. Ribo, you, at page 42, line 24 to 25, you say, and I'm quoting you from the English translation here on the transcript: "I don't recall the El Mujahid Detachment taking part in Operation Vlasic." Now, just bear that in mind. When I turn over to this document that you say was drafted after consultation with you, and about which you say you remember perfectly the contents of paragraph 2.1, can you explain to us what is meant by bullet number 2: "Convey the congratulations of army General Rasim Delic for the success at Vlasic"? To me, it sounds like at the time of drafting this document, the operation at Vlasic had already taken place and it had been successful, and General Delic wants to convey his congratulations to their units. And I assume, because this paragraph deals with the El Mujahid Detachment, it's being conveyed to the El Mujahedin. I see you shaking your head. That's precisely the explanation I would like you to give us. Can you clear up -- clear us up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can clarify. The operation was underway when Paljenik was captured as the top. This is where the radio relay transmitter was, and when the commander of the 7th Corps reported that Opaljenik was captured, this is the initial part of the operation which was very successful. Then General Rasim Delic -- I didn't see the congratulations, but he sent congratulations for those initial successes, but the operation was still ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. You see, you're giving us a long, complicated answer to a very simple question. You don't recall the El Mudjahedin Detachment participating in the Vlasic thing. You have contributed to the drafting of this document, in which, amongst others, General Delic is saying -- conveying congratulations to these people not for Paljenik, for success at Paljenik, but for the success at Vlasic. Now, you're adding "Paljenik" here when the document talks about Vlasic, and this is what I don't understand. Why would they be congratulated for the successes at Vlasic if they refused to take part in the Vlasic operation, because you're saying, as I say, at page 42, line 24 to 25, you don't recall them participating in Operation Vlasic, and yet you are drafting a document here which congratulates them on the success at Vlasic. I want you just to explain that. That's all I'm asking you, a very simple thing. Don't tell me about Paljenik, because Paljenik is not mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My explanation is this: This is a preparatory order. It's not an order specifically to send, but just for the unit to prepare, and there is a difference between an order about the use of a unit and a preparatory order. We are here placing the unit at a certain degree of readiness for the execution of combat actions.
