What is being talked about in the congratulation of Rasim Delic is we -- I, as the person who issued this order, is trying, in the preparation, that they read General Rasim Delic's congratulations at the El Mujahid Detachment about the initial successes at Vlasic, but the Vlasic operation was not completed at that point because it lasted a while longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's a slightly better explanation than the one before, that main point, "Paljenik," with the exclamation. So the congratulations is not for the successes at Vlasic, but it's for the initial success at Vlasic. Again, this document is not stating correctly the facts. I notice that this is now the second document to which you contributed to the drafting of which is not stating the facts correctly, according to your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, just this next question. His Honour has said that this is already the second document that you took part in the drafting, but the facts are incorrect. I would just like to clarify that with you, please. Just one second. Opaljenik, is that a part of Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. It is -- when I was drawing the map, I clearly marked "Opaljenik" because that was the most fortified place in the Vlasic operation. Opaljenik is an integral part and was under the control of the Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. Ribo. So let us continue. Is that the same place, Opaljenik, as the Paljenik location at Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are two different locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now the next thing: Did the El Mudjahedin Detachment take part in these initial actions at all?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this congratulations by General Rasim Delic, does it have anything to do with the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it has nothing to do with them. It was not directed at the El Mudjahedin Detachment but at the units that took part in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this exhibit be given an exhibit number? Oh, it's already been admitted. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing. Mr. Ribo, did you write inaccurate documents during the war?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A mistake, small, minor mistake could slip by, but no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, I would like to look at Exhibit 395. For the transcript, this document is an order of the 3rd Corps Command for preparations to execute a task, and it's dated the 28th of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I would like to ask you: Read this document for yourself, please. It's a short document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please scroll down the English version so that ... You can see this part of the document. And can we also look at the following page of the English version so that the Trial Chamber can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The initials "RH," does that mean that you drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I drafted this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you explain the contents of the document? It's a short document, and it talks about the preparatory order for offensive combat operations to the El Mujahid Detachment, strictly confidential" ... shall cease to be in effect as of 2100 hours on March 28th, 1995." The document we looked at earlier, does that have the same date, the 24th March, 1995? I'm thinking of the preparatory order that we looked at before, and can you please explain the situation?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The corps commander and the chief of staff were angry because the order was not carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous one, the preparatory order that we looked at before. The chief of staff of the 3rd Corps issued a task to me to draft an order of this kind in order to cancel the effectiveness of the previous order, which was the preparatory order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And does this explain the situation, that the El Mudjahedin Detachment did or did not take part in the combat actions?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document indicates that the El Mujahid Detachment did not take part in the combat actions in Vlasic, and that order is being cancelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number? Oh, no, all right, it's already an exhibit. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I would like to ask you this: This paragraph marked "2" of the document states that preparations shall be conducted within the 35th Army Division. Based on what you know, what happened in the next following period with the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to place the detachment in various ways under the control and system of the control and command of the 3rd Corps. However, it was not proceeding very well and we were not succeeding. This paragraph 2, when we're talking about what will happen with the El Mujahid Detachment afterwards, afterwards it was actually placed under the command of the 35th Army Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we please put this document away and look at Exhibit 431. This is a document from the 31st of March, 1995, an order of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who drafted the document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document talks about an order being issued on the resubordination of the detachment to the 35th Division. Please, can you explain to the Trial Chamber what this means? In other words, as of the 31st of March, 1995, who was supposed to command and control this detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll explain. The order is dated the 31st of March, 1995. The El Mujahid Detachment was supposed to enter the 35th Division and be subordinated to the 35th Division commander as of the 1st of April, 1995, from 12.00. It was supposed to report to the 35th Division command post in Zavidovici, and it was to be resubordinated in all matters to the commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please just speak slowly. From what you said, from this point in time that you mentioned, the 1st of April, 1995, who was supposed to be in charge of deploying the detachment in combat?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the commander of the 35th Division and no one else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we put this document away now, unless Their Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I sit back, Mr. Ribo, with the feeling that the resubordination of the El Mujahid Detachment to the 35th Division was decided, I suppose, by General Mahmuljin because he wanted somehow to sanction the 35th -- the El Mujahid Detachment for not having taken part in the Vlasic operation. So I don't know if this is true or not, but could you explain the reasons or do you know about the reasons why the El Mujahid Detachment were resubordinated to the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is difficult to speculate. I suppose that the commander of the 3rd Corps was dissatisfied with their refusing to take part in the operation at Vlasic, and he asked that they be engaged elsewhere, rather than idle away at the barracks or what-not. We tried to place them under somebody's command to do something other than sleep at the barracks and sit on their hands. That's my explanation of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You leave me with the impression that they were somehow seen as being a bit lazy, also, but were they not, at least in other relations, considered to be very brave and courageous soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true, but only at the moment when they said that they were ready to carry out an assignment. If they thought that they were not ready to do that, not a single authority could tell them otherwise, that they should be engaged in an action, be it the commander of the 35th Division, or of the 3rd Corps, or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is very useful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said you want the document put away, Madam Vidovic. You don't want it admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document is Exhibit 431.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you introduced it, you said "document 431", you didn't say "exhibit." That's why.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It is an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, one more question. Could the 3rd Corps commander count on the El Mudjahedin Detachment whenever they needed them in combat?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not count on them, except in situations when they said that they were ready to take part in an action. Otherwise, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should like to move on to a different topic. I'm going to ask you about the events related to the Vozuca theatre of war in the course of 1995. Do you remember, Mr. Ribo, what the thrust of the activities of the Command of the 3rd Corps was in the month of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Did you mean June or July?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question had to do with June, but you can speak both of June and July.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The focus of the activities of the 3rd Corps and its units in the months of June and July of 1995 was the Sarajevo operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long did the operation last, and from when to -- from what date until what date?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation went on from mid-June until mid-July.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in the period you spoke of, including the June and July of 1995, you were assistant chief for operations and training, and you said, whilst describing your duties, that it included the planning of combat activities of the units of the 3rd Corps. Did the Command of the 3rd Corps plan combat activities in the July of 1995 in the Ozren-Vozuca pocket or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who planned those combat activities?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 35th Division. The focus of my planning and that of the 3rd Corps was directed at the Sarajevo operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the 3rd Corps command over these combat activities?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was within the competence of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who deployed the units that were to take part in the combat activities in the July of 1995, including the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the Command of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just clarify that. When you talk about those July operations, are you referring to the Ozren-Vozuca operations or the Sarajevo operations, because now we have got two operations taking place at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, when I asked you about who it was who gave assignments or deployed the units that were involved in the combat activities in the July of 1995, I meant the Ozren-Vozuca front. Do you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the Command of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you take any part in the Vozuca operation in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were at the Command of the 3rd Corps also in September of 1995. Did the corps have any combat activities in the Ozren-Vozuca pocket at the time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you engaged in any activities related to that particular combat action, and, if so, of what sort?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: By virtue of my function, according to the establishment, I was charged with drafting combat documents related to the September operation, i.e., Operation Farz. Once the combat documents were drafted, the units were deployed to the area close to Vozuca. My task was, in addition to planning combat activities, to monitor combat activities, analyse them, to stay over there and organise activities such as work at the command post, work in subordinate units, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will take it one step at a time. You said that you participated in planning the action. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 380. Your Honours, this is the large map pertaining to Action Farz. I don't know if you have it before you, because the one that has been scanned is not visible. Can the witness be given this map. We sent an e-mail, informing about the use of this map. Perhaps the map could be placed on the ELMO. Mr. Ribo, have a look at the map, and first of all did I show you this map and did you have a very close look at it during proofing?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you showed me this map, and I did go through it carefully.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the map again. Did you have occasion to see that map earlier on?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I made it with my assistants, especially with the draftsman, and he and I are authors of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please zoom in on the part of the map where markings have been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could I just be orientated, Madam Vidovic. Are we now dealing with the September operation and have we left the July operation?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We are discussing Operation Farz from September and the map of Plan Farz. Can we zoom in on the bottom half of the map, where a number of markings were made. That's fine, very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, tell us what the Plan Farz represents.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan represents the decision of the commander to engage all units participating in the offensive operation with specific axes of attack, next attack, following attack, immediate attack, or tasks, that is, and it is -- specifies which of the units will take part in which part of the action, along which axes and with units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned units. Which are the units that are given this assignment by the Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this operation, the Corps issued assignments to the following units: 1st Manoeuvre Battalion --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, pause there. We can see that some markings were made. I meant the degree of subordination. In those terms, can you tell us which units were involved?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the units immediately subordinated to the unit issuing order for the operation. Therefore, immediately subordinated to the Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And which were those units immediately subordinated, in principle?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you on this map which were the units immediately subordinated to the 3rd Corps in this operation; namely, the 1st Manoeuvre Battalion, 375th Liberation Brigade, 7th Chivalrous Muslim Liberation Brigade, the 5th Battalion of the 303rd Chivalrous Brigade, the 35th Division of the Land Forces, and of course there were units attached to the staff that were either of temporary structure or a permanent structure, such as an artillery regiment, logistics, communications, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did the General Staff have a role to play in relation to this plan or not? I'm referring to Plan Farz. I'm referring actually to the map of Farz.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The preparation, drafting and distribution of the map did not in any way involve the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the General Staff have any other role to play, in terms of approval, for instance?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The map was only approved by the General Staff. That's the extent of their involvement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the map. From where I look at it, I believe it's the top left corner that we're interested in. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the General Staff issued their approval. Do you see General Delic's name here?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is pretty blurred, but we did say in the heading that it says: "I approve, commander of the army, General Rasim Delic."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to this map that was approved by the General Staff, was any sort of task given to the El Mujahid Detachment or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no assignment at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the commander of the General Staff did not engage in such minor matters as issuing orders to units at such a low level. He would issue orders to corps commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were involved in the planning of Operation Farz. Did any of those documents mention a role to be played by the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the direct command was the 35th Division, and pursuant to an earlier order, the El Mudjahedin Detachment was subordinated to the 35th Division. We had no reason to issue orders directly to the El Mudjahedin Detachment, since they were under the 35th Division and we would issue orders to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. If Their Honours don't have any questions regarding this map, you can take it away, and I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 461, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you see here whether this document has been approved or not, or had been approved?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document had not been approved, and it is not signed by the corps commander. There is no stamp, either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Could we now look at page 17 of this document. That's in B/C/S version. That's a map, an integral part of this document, Your Honours. But could we perhaps rotate it, because it is fairly difficult to look at it the way it is now - yes, very well, thank you - so that we can see the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see whether this map was approved in this form by the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map was not approved or certified by a seal of the 3rd Corps, and I assume this was perhaps some draft version of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you a question. As a rule, when -- or, rather, such decisions at the division level, decisions of the division commander, are they submitted to the commander of the General Staff for his approval ever?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. If the division is under the command of the 3rd Corps, this decision has nothing to do with the commander of the General Staff. But if the division is directly subordinated to the General Staff, then it has to submit it there. But this was not the case now, because this division was part of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We can put this document away. Now I would like this witness to look at Exhibit 389. For the record, this is a document of the 3rd Corps from the forward command post at Luke. The date is the 8th of September, 1995. The heading is: "Team for direct command and control of the offensive operation F," "Farz." I would like you to look at this document, and could -- could the witness please look at page 2 of this document. That's page 3 in the English version. Page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We can see the initials "RH" on this document. Would those be your initials? Did you work on this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, what is the gist of this document? What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this document or this order indicates who should be at what position in the course of the operation, so this is a disposition of the personnel from the 3rd Corps Command, indicating where they are to be in the course of the operation to provide some kind of support to the subordinate commands and units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please now go back to page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I would like to ask you to look at paragraph 3 of this document. Is your name stated there, paragraph 3? Could we please scroll this document down for Their Honours so that they can look at paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my name is mentioned in paragraph 3, and also some other persons who are to accompany me to the forward command post of the 35th Division located in Babilon Restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at page 2 of this document, paragraph 10. That's at page 2 both in Bosnian and the English versions, paragraph 10. It is indicated here: "The headquarters Administration commander shall provide dry rations for the officers assigned to units for a minimum of three days and remove those officers from the list of users of supplies at the IKM Luke." What did this mean?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It meant that we would work there for three days and that we were supposed to take dry rations with us, because we could not be a burden to the subordinate units in the course of such actions. They were not supposed to look after us and to provide food for us, and that is why we received the dry rations from our unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The gist of my question is as follows: Did you spend those three days at Babilon, at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent two days there, and my associates were there for three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. What would be the dates, the two dates?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 10th and the 11th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can put this document away now. And now I would like the witness to look at a very brief document. That would be Exhibit 403. For the record, this is an order from the 2nd Corps Command, dated the 1st of September, 1995, about the dispatching of a team of 2nd Corps officers from the forward command post to the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you whether the 3rd BH Army Corps was the only formation participating in those actions.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The troops from the 3rd and the 2nd Corps participated together in this action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did anyone coordinate the actions? And if yes, could you please tell us how this was done?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody coordinated those actions on the part of the General Staff. This responsibility and this obligation was taken up by the 2nd and the 3rd Corps, and we, ourselves, organised coordinated action by the two corps in this action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I want you to look at this document. What is this document all about? Could you please zoom in a little bit so that we can see. That's fine, so that the witness can read.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this document indicates that the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps, or, rather, the commander of the 2nd Corps notifies us in this document and actually issues an order to his subordinates that a team from another formation would come to our forward command post, headed by Brigadier Sulejman Budakovic, and that we should deal with all the issues related to combat that was some ten days before the operation, on the very eve of the operation, in other words. And it is specified where and when they would show up so that we could arrange everything for successful, coordinated action by the two units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I think that this is a convenient time for a break, so I would like to stop at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. While we go for the break, Madam Vidovic, you might perhaps want to contemplate the fact that the Defence is left with five minutes to complete its four hours. We'll take a break and come back at -- yes, you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The only thing I can say is that I will need more time. You will understand, we all had many questions for this witness. I will do my best, but if I go over the time that I was allotted, I will not be asking any questions. I will try to address some issues with other witnesses. So I will be within the time, but I don't think that I can complete my examination within five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll talk about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may simply before we break, just in terms of planning, I would not expect the cross-examination of this witness to take more than 75 minutes, a normal court session, just in terms of planning in terms of the overall schedule for this week. So I thought I would just indicate that at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We were talking about the events at Vozuca regarding Operation Farz, and I would like us to dwell on this topic for a little while longer. So my question is the following: To your knowledge, did the Supreme Command Staff play any role in any of these operations or activities?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no role at all. In fact, from the moment of the planning until the end of this operation, no officer from that staff appeared there at the front or did assist the units and commands in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A little while ago, you mentioned -- but before that, let me ask you this: Halid Cengic, do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, did you see him during Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him there, but he did not -- he was not present there as a representative of the General Staff units. He just came to see Mahmuljin to congratulate him on his success at the Vozuca front.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what job did he have at that time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a logistics officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. When you say, "Yes, I did see him there, but he was not present there as a representative," there where?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Halid with General Mahmuljin, the 3rd Corps commander, at the command post, so this was not on the first or the second day of the offensive, but at a later period. That was at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Forward command post of ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said a little while ago that on the 11th of September, you were at the forward command post of the 35th Division at Babilon. On that date, were you in contact with Fadil Hasanagic, the commander of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you receive any information from Mr. Hasanagic or anyone else regarding any prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that date or at any date later during the operation did I receive any such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about the El Mudjahedin Detachment kidnapping some 60 prisoners from the 328th Division?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again, when I asked the question, my question was whether, on that date, you received information or not, and the words "or not" were not recorded in the transcript, so let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So did you hear anything about any abductions of the members -- or, rather, prisoners of war from the 328th Division?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear anything about that. I was the third-highest-ranking person in the corps, and this Tribunal did not exist at the time, so I should have received this information in my capacity as the third-highest-ranking officer in the corps, but I never did receive any such information, I never heard anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown D1023. For the record, this is an excerpt from the book of minutes of the briefings at the forward command post. The date is the 22nd of August until the 9th of September, 1995. So that's the period covered by it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before we look at the relevant page, let me just ask you: Did I show you this document in the proofing sessions for your testimony here, and did you inspect it in detail?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to see page 2, both in English and in Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, Madam Vidovic, just can we go back to page 1 of the Bosnian, of the B/C/S, please. Thank you. On the B/C/S, Madam Vidovic, you will see there's a handwritten entry there from 22nd August, 1995, to some date. We don't have anything written on the English. Are you able to tell us what is that date?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way I see it -- uh-huh, yes, I can. In the Bosnian version it says from the 22nd of August, 1995, until the 9th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the 9th, not the 6th? Okay, thank you. You may proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to look at page 2 of this document, both in the Bosnian and the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to look at the date, the 11th of September, 1995, and you can see that this is a meeting apparently held at 1530 hours. Is that so, Witness?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We see a list of persons present at the briefing, the briefing to the 3rd Corps commander. Here we can see the commander of the NS, and then NONP. What does "NONP" stand for?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the chief of the -- of the section for -- well, I really don't know. I think that's the chief of the section for training/planning, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Is that the function that you held?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is supposed to be my post.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please center this document in such a way that we can see the last sentence on this page. We can see it in the English version. Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read the last sentence on this page? Can you see that it says: "War booty. Problem with the El Mujahid needs to be solved." Could you please tell us, what was this all about, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. This was the report when the commander of the 375th said at this briefing that he had difficulties with the El Mujahid concerning war booty. It practically boiled down to a conflict that broke out between the members of the 375th Brigade and the El Mujahid Detachment, and I know this because I remember this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we turn to page 3 of the document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you turn to -- sorry, can we go back again? I'm sorry, Madam Vidovic. I just want to get clarity on a little point. After the number "3", there is a sentence that says: "Commander. President congratulated." Who is referred to by "president"? Who are we referring to there when we say "president"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that a question addressed to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, it is addressed to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This relates to the commander of the 3rd Corps, where it says "The president," and this refers to the President Alija Izetbegovic, who congratulated them on a successful most probably action - it doesn't say - and that soon he would visit Modrica. In other words, the corps commander conveys this information to us who were at this briefing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we turn to page 3 of the document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to the first line. It says: "Captured Adem Kurtic from Banja Luka, a Chetnik who was captured this morning." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the part mentioning Rekic, war booty? I will read the second sentence somewhere in the middle of the sentence. The second sentence says: "War booty. Known [Realtime transcript read in error "no"] problem with the El Mujahid. Five killed, Sehids, and ten wounded. 37 Chetniks were killed." Let me ask you this: At the briefings to the corps commander, was it a customary procedure to brief on both the enemy soldiers who were killed and those who were captured?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a customary practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does this, what Mr. Rekic said, meant about the 37 Chetniks having been killed? How did he explain this? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that along his access of attack, he registered or observed 37 soldiers of Republika Srpska who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You speak of 33 or 37 soldiers? It says "37" here.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were killed how? Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He reported on the losses suffered by the other side, and that's something that every unit keeps note of.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the last sentence here, please, the last sentence of the Bosnian version. Can it be please displayed on the screen? Can we move to that part of the page? Do you see that it says: "Ended at 1650"? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this, please: At the time of the briefing, was the commander of the 3rd Corps informed in any way about any other prisoners of war, except for the one mentioned here, Adem Kurtic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My understanding is that you were at the Babilon IKM where the commander of the 35th Division, Hasanagic, was present too. If you had heard anything about war prisoners, would it have been your duty to report on this at the meeting of the commanders or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be logical for me to report on any individuals captured, if any were captured, that is. However, I didn't have any information to that effect, and I could not speak off the top of my head about information I didn't have reliable sources about or wasn't sure of.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the next page of the document. Here, too, the briefing of the 3rd Corps commander is mentioned on the 12th of September. However, this time we have a different time indicated. What is it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the document. Were you present at this briefing or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go carefully through the entire page now. Mr. Ribo, at this briefing, was this information concerning the 60-odd prisoners captured by the Mujahedin Detachment ever mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sure it can, but I have a few questions relating to it before we get to the admission. If I may turn back to the previous page - thank you - because, Madam Vidovic, you read out a part from the middle where it says: "War prize: Known problem with the El Mujahid," and, "Five killed ..." This came out in the transcript as "no problem with the Mujahid," and I just wanted to point to this correction so that we get the transcript right. Now, my question to the witness is: There was apparently a known problem with the Mujahid, and you have made one reference to it a little earlier. What was the problem, the known problem with the Mujahid, in relation to war prize, or booty, or prisoners, or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After our units completed the immediate task, I left the command post of the 35th Division and set out in a motor vehicle to follow our units in the direction of Vozuca. Along that route, there's the village called "Stog." In the middle of our activities, the Serb forces withdrew from Stog, leaving behind a warehouse full of ammunition and weapons. It had not been either mined or taken away. As I came there, I saw that the fighters of the Rekic's unit clashed with foreigners. I wasn't able to ascertain at the time that they were, indeed, the El Mujahid, but I assumed, since they were along that same axis of attack, that they had clashed over war booty. Since I wasn't able to solve the problem, I summoned Commander Rekic to deal with that conflict in the village of Stog.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So we are to understand that the problems that have been referred to several times in this document were only about the seizure of ammunition left behind by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, but it's a war booty, materiel and technical equipment, i.e., ammunition, weapons, explosives, communications equipment and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. But no prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not at all. It didn't involve prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ribo. How was the conflict or the problem with this ammunition and other booty, how was that eventually solved? Did Rekic's unit finally get hold of it, or did the EMD take it, or what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rekic appeared as a commander of that unit, and he withdrew his fighters, leaving the war booty over to the others, probably members of the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And was that the end of the story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, that was the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, one more question on this issue. Could any of you order the El Mujahid to give the war booty back to Rekic's unit?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody was able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this document be assigned an exhibit now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1189.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we put this document away now and show the witness Exhibit 512. To save time, can we move right away to page 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What we see here, Mr. Ribo, is "War Diary." So page 19 of the Bosnian and page 13 of the English version. Mr. Ribo, please look at the part of the document relating to the 11th of September, 1995, which says: "New line axis of attack within the AOR of the 35th Division and new assignments of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, and the 2nd Man-Bat are attacking and taking Kvrge," and so on and so forth, and it says 10 -- another 10 square kilometres of territory was liberated, a second 10 was captured, and some 60 Chetniks were killed and 57 captured. So this talks of the capture of Serb soldiers. Were you informed of this particular entry of the war diary, and was this same information conveyed elsewhere in a report, at a briefing, to a commander, or anywhere else where it would have reached you?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had this been the case, indeed, it should have been mentioned in the oral briefing to the commander, and it should have been forwarded to the superior command or it should have reached us from the subordinated unit, that's to say from the 35th Division. The information should have reached us of the existence of prisoners. I had never heard anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we put the document away now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry. Remind us, who is the author of this diary?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the war diary of the 3rd Corps. Perhaps the witness would be better placed to say something. This is a document that was admitted into evidence and was tendered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you assist us in telling us who could be the author of the document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably, since one of my officers entered the information into this war diary, the author of the diary is Safet Sivro. He would enter the information at a later date, after the event transpired. It did not have to be necessarily contemporaneous. I had never heard this information about the captured Serb individuals, truly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a follow-up question. Did Safet Sivro ever inform you of this?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The war diary, is that a document that the Command would necessarily read?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A war diary is more like a historical document that histories can be written. I didn't read it, no one else actually read it. The corps commander didn't read it. I don't know anyone of actually reading it. It was just things were written in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. If I may, you said the author of this diary was Safet Sivro. Just to get clarity, was he the author of the diary or was he the author of the entry of the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's the author of entries of this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand you to say that all entries in the diary are entered by one person and one person only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Several people entered the data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Therefore, we cannot then say Safet Sivro is the author of the diary. We can say he's one of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, that is correct. I perhaps misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know who made this entry of the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judging by the handwriting, I think that it was Safet Sivro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, as you sit there, nothing has ever been done by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina about these alleged 57 captured prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing. I don't even know that to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, then, they just must have disappeared into thin air?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness very clearly, in response to a number of my questions, said that he had never heard of these 57 prisoners, that he never heard of them, so I cannot understand how the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina would have done anything if the witness didn't hear of it. The witness Sivro was here, and this question was not put to him, from what I can remember, and this is why I wanted to put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand, and I just wanted to clear that, so that if the army didn't do anything about it, then we know. What was your answer, sir? You said you really don't know. Okay, I understand. Thank you so much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this document away now. And can we show the witness document D1009. For the transcript, this is a study on the organisation of routine duty at the Forward Command Post 3, Luke, from August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you if you've seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this document before, and I also worked on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain to us what the objective of this document was, if you know, and if there was any objective?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective of this document was to regulate precisely the working life of people in the 3rd Corps Command at the forward command post of Luke, because we were leaving the command post and forming a forward command post. And at this place where the Command would be working, living and commanding, the document regulates duty shifts, guard shifts, the duty driver and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the witness now please look at page 3 of the Bosnian version and the fourth page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is signed by the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to the next page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, it seems that we have a kind of form here. Can you please look at it and tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This kind of form is the attachment to the document that we looked at earlier, the study, and it is stated specifically here this is the template for the person who would be making the reports on the matters that they would be informing the Bosnia and Herzegovina Main Command from the forward command post at Kakanj, and to the 3rd Corps as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please pay attention to paragraph marked "2," and tell us whether or not information needed to be furnished about important results or problems in the day that had to do with combat activities? Did this have to be sent to the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the main question. The basic information had to be sent to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would this or would it not include the information about prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have to include that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at page 5 now of the Bosnian version and page 7 of the English version. Can you please look at paragraph 6, "Security Situation" or "Security Status." On the basis of this part of the document, would the information have to be provided or not on the number of detained persons, captured persons, arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information would have to be provided, because the security sector was in charge of these questions, because this is clearly regulated in the commander's command for Farz, the Operation Farz, the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we're looking at this document, this instruction on the manner of supplying information, was this something that was received by the subordinate units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to report on the basis of the same elements to the IKM of the 3rd Corps at Luke.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the commander of the 3rd Corps, did he issue precise reporting instructions also in reference to prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did that in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document becomes Exhibit number 1190.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to deal with the last topic with you now. It has to do with record-keeping documents. You mentioned that you worked on documents and records. So just briefly, can you please tell Their Honours exactly what these documents were? What included these record-keeping documents?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Daily report books, operations diaries, book of briefings, the diary from the observation point. These are all the documents that are part of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. In your work, did you get access to these documents, did you have anything to do with them, and if you did, in which way?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have access to these documents, but my job was mainly, in my department, to conduct the pagination of these documents, because these were classic notebooks, to organise them in a practical way, to number them and to enter them, and then after entering them, to send them to the people who were using them for their further use.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you numbered them, can you please tell us exactly what that means?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that each page had to be numbered, starting from the ordinal number 1 until the end, depending on the number of pages that the book had.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "page"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the front and back of the page, so both sides of a page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have asked my colleagues from the OTP to show this witness the original Exhibit 511, and thanks to the kindness of the Prosecution, they did provide this original. So during the break, the witness examined in detail that exhibit. I would like to ask the Prosecutor now to also give this document for the perusal of the witness. We're talking about Exhibit 511.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can you please tell us whether you looked at the document during the break?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what was your role in relation to this document? Can you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in regard to this document, it was my job to paginate the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, to paginate?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means to write precisely the number of pages in ink, starting from the ordinal number 1 until the end of the book, depending on the number of pages that the book had.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the usher to help the witness to place specific pages on the ELMO so that Their Honours can see that, as well as the other parties in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the number, please? Can you place the document on the ELMO and show us the number that you would enter? When you say that you did the pagination, what did you write in?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are the numbers in the upper right-hand corner [indicates], number 1, number 2, number 3, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just stop there for a minute. So the page has the number 1, then the next page is empty, and then the page after that has the next number?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why -- I'm going to ask you to look at the last page now, and if you can place it on the ELMO, the last page. I don't know if we have it. We should also have it in English. Your Honours, this is a document tendered by the Prosecution. Witness, can you please read slowly what it says here, what it says here on this last page, slowly?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "This notebook has 95 pages, as stated and certified by the chief of the Department for Operations and Training, Colonel Haso Ribo." And there's my signature there and a stamp, and it says: "Record book number 35."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now can you please tell us, why does it say: "Record book number 35" here?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was a special register, a protocol, where all these books were entered, the number under which they were issued and how many pages each notebook has.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You told us that you looked at this diary during the break. Does that have 95 pages? Can you please tell us what you remarked about this original document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document does not have 95 pages, as stated here. I noticed, from page 19 up to 95, there are no paginated pages, and you can see clearly from the document that it was handled and that the pages were torn out or removed in some other way from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now ask the usher, please, to place the relevant pages on the ELMO. Can you please find the page you mentioned, page 19?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, page 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you say about it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From page 19 until page 91, the pages are not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, when you certified and signed the document, did you number or paginate this notebook yourself, personally?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what is your conclusion, now that you've looked at it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that the document was handled or tampered with, because practically the way it was paginated and certified, pages could not have been added or ripped out from this document or any other document. What I remark here is that the documents from the 9th of October, 1995, onwards are missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, I don't know whether this is a question of translation. The English translation says: "I assumed that the document was handled or tampered with, because practically the way it was paginated and certified, pages could not have been added or ripped out from this document ..." Now, the fact of the matter is you are telling us that pages were ripped out of the document, but if you're saying they could not be, you're telling us of an impossibility, but it has happened. Are you able to explain why it happened, if it is impossible for it to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None of the persons entering information into this notebook could have added anything, or anyone else could have added or taken pages out, and we can see, in the original document that I have here, that a large number of pages is missing. This should not have been allowed to happen. The person who had the book should not have been permitted to add or to rip out any pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The correct answer, then, should have been: Pages should not have been added or ripped out. That's what you meant to say. Thank you. I don't know, maybe that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As I say, it may be a problem of translation. Thank you so much. Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You can put away the document. Actually, you can return it to the Prosecutor. At this point, I would like to ask the witness to look at the original of Exhibit 394.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Ribo, did you have an opportunity to look at the document during the break?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have a chance to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. First of all, can you please show us page 1? Can you place it on the ELMO? First of all, I would like to ask you this: Did you work also on this document? Did you apply the same procedure that you described earlier, the pagination and the signature?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the identical procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please show us page 1. Very well. Page 2. Very well. Now I would like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we interrupt a little bit? It looks like -- can we excuse Judge Lattanzi. Thank you very much. From now on, for the remainder of the session, the Chamber will sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Thank you very much. You may proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when we're talking about ordinal numbers in this document, do they go -- would these ordinal numbers have to begin from 1 and then until the last number indicating the end of this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Are you talking about the first column? Yes, the ordinal numbers should go in sequence from 1 to N, the Nth number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now can you please find -- leaf through the document and look at page -- find the number 66, 66. One lower. Very well, very well. And now let's move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Maybe I'm not looking at the same thing, but I'm not seeing number 66 on what is before me. On the B/C/S side -- that's better, now I begin to see "66" on the B/C/S side. I don't see it on the English side. Can we be shown 66 on the English side, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English page is 15, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just interested in the entry number 66, whatever page it comes on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you look at the top of this page? In fact, I invite Your Honour to look at the very top of this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of which page, ma'am, English or --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 15, 15 in the English version, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can't see the page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm still looking for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps we can -- okay, yes, it's there, so we can see it now. Page 15 in the English version. It was on the screen just a moment ago. Please, that's the page. I hope, Your Honours, that now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We do see entry number 66, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to place the original of the page on the ELMO, the page with the date the 15th of September. Witness, should the numbers for the next day run from 67, 68, and so on?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is the situation like in the original?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of the 15th of September starts with 1, and then we go on to 2, 3, until 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had paginated this document, and do you know what the practice is regarding the numbering of such documents? Is this the usual practice?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not seeing the top of -- the entry of the 15th on the ELMO. That's better.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 15th. Your Honours, I don't know if you see it right below this, the first box here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The point you are making is that from the 15th, instead of 67, we have one; that's the point you are making? Thank you very --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, as you yourself have just commented, is that the regular procedure; can this be done in this way?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not the regular procedure, it's not proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look -- okay, so we've seen page 15. Could we now go to page 12 in the Bosnian version of this document. It's page 12 in the English version, too. Let's leave page 15 here in English, and let's move to page 12 in the Bosnian version. Page 15 in the English is fine, but let us look at page 12 in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, this is a bit confusing. When we had the entry number 66 in the Bosnian version, I think the time was 1837 or something of that kind, and in the English version the entry 66 is 1905. I'm just wondering if the two entries are really the same or if we're speaking about two different entries, both of which have number 66.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can look at page 10, and then everything will be clear, page 10 in the Bosnian version. So please leave the English version as it stands, and let's move to page 10 in the Bosnian version. Now, Your Honours, right at the bottom you can see an entry in the Bosnian language, which is identical to the one in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Witness, could you please read the entry under number 66?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that: "The commander of the 7th Chivalrous Muslim Liberation Brigade arrived at the 3rd Corps forward command post."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Do you see that now, Your Honours? Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this document, I would like to ask you this question: Were you able to leaf through the whole document, and does this document --

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did leaf through it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 32 in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Were you able to leaf through," to page through? The English says "leaf" as in a leaf. Did you mean by that to page through the book?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, I just wanted to understand what you ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I say 32 of the Bosnian version, I'm referring to the page 32 of this exhibit. Now, in the original, we have a different pagination because of the way in which the Prosecutor uploaded it as an exhibit. Now, we have in front of us -- unfortunately, Your Honours, this exhibit has been uploaded in such a way that this part of the document was not translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read what it says here in the Bosnian version?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this is the document that I have in front of me, then it says: "Communications documents for concerted action with the HVO units."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the communications documents, do they exist in the original of the document that you saw?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they exist. But the communications documents for the concerted action with the HVO units, are they part of this document at all, on any basis? Can they be an integral part of that document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They cannot be an integral part of this document, because I explained right at the beginning nothing can be inserted, nothing can be removed from those record books, if it is not paginated or numbered. So all those documents that were inserted or added should not have been inserted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do those documents have anything to do with the main topic in the diary?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, the communications documents are documents that pertain to the communications organ, and they had nothing to do with this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Madam Vidovic, for being a bit confused. The document we see here on the screen, "Dokumenta Veze," was that -- I'm sorry for asking, but was that the same document that we had with the entry number 66?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And was that document the war diary or, as I understood, the operations diary of the army -- of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the operations diary of the observation post of the commander. That's the title of this document: "Operations Diary of the Commander's Observation Post."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And again forgive me for not having all the evidence completely clear for me, but the war diary or the operations diary of the 3rd Corps was also the document in which we found a while ago the entry about 57 prisoners of war; is that correct? So it's the same document we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, it's not the same document. The previous one was the war diary, and this is the operations diary. But it is a record, but it's not the same document. Both documents are records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm very happy that I asked these questions, because otherwise I would have not understood. So the war diary is one record, and that contains a single notion about 57 prisoners of war. The operations diary is another record made by the same corps, the 3rd Corps, and this latter operations diary does not contain any reference to the prisoners of war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know at this moment. I focused mostly on the authenticity, so I'm not sure at this time. I will look into that, and I owe you an answer, but I really focused on the authenticity of this document. I wanted to verify whether this is an authentic document or whether the document has been tampered with. That was the thrust of the questions that I asked, whether any pages were modified, inserted. So I didn't go into the contents of the document, so anything that I would tell you at this point would be -- I believe that nothing is mentioned about those prisoners, but -- I think not, but that would be -- at any rate, this is a Prosecution exhibit. It was admitted as a Prosecution exhibit, and I challenged the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, I accept that there is a problem of its authenticity, for the reasons that we have seen and discussed several times during this trial, but what I'm interested in and what I think is crucial for the Chamber to learn is to know which source to consult for the record of the daily operations and events that occurred in the units falling under the 3rd Corps' authority, and I understand that some -- let me just please finish my question. I understand that some of the record was made in the war diary and other information was entered into the operations diary. And may I add, apparently the operations diary only dealt with the encounters with the HVO. That's what it says on the title. So -- but this may be wrong, but I want the witness now to tell us, in which sources were the entries made for each day at the 3rd Corps level? My expectation is that there has to be at least one document where you would find evidence of what occurred during the day for each of the units of the 3rd Corps, including the 3rd Corps itself. Now, can you tell us, at the 3rd Corps level, where you were, what was the source that was created reflecting the daily events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the operations diary of the command post or of the forward command post, and this is the operations diary of the observation post. So during the operation, the commander was at the observation post, forwarding him an overview of what is happening at the front, and this records what happened at the commander's observation post in the course of combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But this would be -- forgive me for not understanding this. I, unfortunately, have no battle experience myself. Or maybe I should say "fortunately so." The operations diary from this observation post, that would be only part of the information that was collected during the day from the 3rd Corps, meaning that there would be other observation posts from other parts of the front line which also would have an operations diary, and by the end of the day, the information entered in each of these different operations diaries would then be entered into either the war diary or some other document at the 3rd Corps Command, or is that a misrepresentation of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The operations diary of an observation post, a location where the commander is, all the information is received via the phone or radio equipment, not -- nothing is received in writing. He receives information from the -- via communications equipment so that he could, at any -- at an opportune time, issue some orders to his subordinates. And regular reports were sent to the forward command post from the unit commands, and this forward command post was located at Luke. So this is just some of the information that was relevant at that time for the commander to be able to exercise command during the operation. It was relayed using radio communications or communications equipment, and it was sent using other means to the forward command post at Luke, and then we sent it on to the command -- forward command post of the General Staff at Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sure we will pursue this tomorrow also, but let me just put one final question to you. The forward command post in Kakanj would also have a diary reflecting the main events of the day, would it not? And if so, what was that document called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I was not at the General Staff command post. I did not hold any posts in the General Staff, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I thought you were chief of staff. Were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the chief of the department for monitoring combat operations. I was the chief of staff at a later stage, when the war was over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have the original now, and so that the Prosecution does not have to bring it back again tomorrow. Just one more question, if you allow me. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you notice whether all the dates in September are listed here in this diary? What happens with the dates between the 10th and the 15th of September? Are they listed in the diary?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, there are no records for the 6th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when do they restart?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they don't. The rest of the pages are blank. And I was also able to ascertain that in the middle part, some pages are missing, pages from 18 through 42. So you see here we have number 19 [indicates], and all the pages until page 42 are missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. That's all I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, if I may just get clarity, you said you paginate these books, don't you -- didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, just tell us what you -- you just put in the pagination or did you also make the entries in the book, that book in front of you, in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was my task to open the document, to paginate it, to sign it, and to give it to other people for their use. So I didn't make any entries in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clears me. We'll take an adjournment and come back tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of March, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
